Lysosomal storage disorder; skeletal dysplasia/joint restriction and neurologic impairment are common (~30%+) across major forms. Functionally damaging eye disease varies by subtype.

Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic defect; neurologic damage is common, with ataxia in 3/3 and cerebellar vermis atrophy in 2/2 assessed.
Primary megaureter is a structural and functional ureteral disorder; ureters belong to the renal axis.

Autoimmune muscle necrosis; pharyngoesophageal muscle dysfunction causes frequent dysphagia (30-79%). Interstitial lung disease and myocarditis occur below 30%.

Hereditary peripheral neuropathy with parkinsonism and defining eyelid ptosis; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.

Apert-like craniosynostosis and limb malformations with polydactyly define the syndrome; no evidence establishes additional commonly damaged organs.
